# selinux / binpolicy-fuzzer

selinux's own fuzz target `binpolicy-fuzzer` ([source](source/binpolicy-fuzzer.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over selinux (SELinuxProject/selinux at efd1aa51).

Checks 2 properties (listed below); the first, an invariant: A kernel policy that policydb_read accepted must still pass policydb_validate after policydb_optimize (optimisation preserves validity).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against selinux at commit efd1aa51.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- A kernel policy that policydb_read accepted must still pass policydb_validate after policydb_optimize (optimisation preserves validity) ([line 53](source/binpolicy-fuzzer.c#L53)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Any binary policy that was read successfully must be writable (policydb_write) and, for kernel policies, convertible to policy.conf and CIL; module/base policies must convert to CIL; an expanded base must also write and convert ([lines 69-107](source/binpolicy-fuzzer.c#L69-L107)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch selinux` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `binpolicy-fuzzer.plain` | 346,192 | `3d35e58226aab8c4c8bfaf788e6c9bdafcf1652ecfae0f3037a8a827678effc1` |
| ubsan | `binpolicy-fuzzer.ubsan` | 411,056 | `5f7b82a0ef527ebdd8ff7667956199ab7bf8d8a80301b764dc39d27ad1653170` |
| asan | `binpolicy-fuzzer.asan` | 1,476,184 | `c698a244ef48f1f58c40ee669652901d5815be8c1aa87329e8871e4e5ac9340f` |
| asan-ubsan | `binpolicy-fuzzer.asan-ubsan` | 1,535,704 | `8744baf6344f02b7802c9538f81ca3816156381808cd0a5a6a02b164c98e897a` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
